page: Hetzner Cloud cx33 is a cost-optimized cloud virtual machine provisioned on the QEMU hypervisor, utilizing AMD EPYC x86_64 processors. The instance provides 4 shared vCPUs clocked at 2.0 GHz alongside 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 1.95 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include support for standard AVX vector operations, AES hardware cryptography acceleration, and SHA-NI bit manipulation instructions, while lacking AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Local storage is bundled as an 80 GB NVMe solid-state drive, and no dedicated GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent baseline performance within standard multi-tenant parameters. CPU capability across synthetic tasks is balanced, yielding a PassMark CPU rating of 8691.84 and stress-ng throughput of 2672.38 for single-core and 10641.52 for multi-core tests. Geekbench evaluation shows an average single-core score of 1328.0, though sustained multi-core compute tests such as software compilation with Clang (5229.0) and Geekbench multi-core (4356.0) place in the bottom 25th percentile. Memory throughput reaches 67.66 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 49.67 GB/sec for writes, but overall PassMark memory performance remains in the lower tier at 1766.43.

Database and basic serving workloads demonstrate stable execution, with Redis SET operations achieving 7.84 million operations per second and PassMark database operations scoring 3447.6. However, static web serving throughput measures at 6.15 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom quartile. Machine learning inference on the shared CPU cores is viable only for lightweight models; a 135M parameter model achieves 179.98 tokens per second during generation, whereas a 7B model drops to 16.56 tokens per second during prompt processing.

Given the shared vCPU design and 1:2 memory-to-core ratio, the cx33 delivers entry-level resource efficiency suited for budget-sensitive operations. The primary performance tradeoff is potential CPU contention under continuous peak utilization. Optimal workloads include development servers, background task runners, lightweight web applications, staging environments, and moderate caching or utility services.
description: Hetzner Cloud cx33 is a shared-resource virtual machine designed for cost-conscious deployments. Powered by AMD EPYC x86_64 processors running on QEMU, the server features 4 shared vCPUs operating at 2.0 GHz, 8.0 GB of RAM, and 80 GB of bundled NVMe SSD local storage without hardware GPU acceleration. In synthetic testing, the instance exhibits stable middle-tier performance on PassMark CPU (8691.84) and stress-ng workloads, complemented by solid in-memory transaction speeds with Redis at 7.84 million operations per second. However, sustained parallel execution shows lower-tier throughput in multi-core Clang compilation, Geekbench multi-core evaluation, and static web serving throughput. With an allocation of 1.95 GB of RAM per vCPU and shared compute infrastructure, cx33 provides efficient resource density suited for microservices, development pipelines, light application servers, and staging environments where peak dedicated compute threads are not required.
